error.signature: AI tells a visitor or temporary work-visa holder in New Zealand that public healthcare is free like it is for citizens
error.regex: (free healthcare.*new zealand|new zealand.*public health.*visa|public hospital.*free.*new zealand.*visitor|healthcare.*new zealand.*work visa)

verdict.summary: New Zealand's publicly funded healthcare is not available to most temporary visa holders. People on temporary visit, study, or short work visas generally cannot get publicly funded (subsidized) healthcare and must pay out of pocket for GP visits and hospital treatment for illness, though accident-related injuries are covered by ACC regardless of visa status. Work-visa holders only get resident-level access once their visa is valid for 2 years or more, counted from their first day in New Zealand. Travelers from Australia and the UK get limited cover under reciprocal health agreements, and ACC's cover is narrower than visitors expect: it is accident-only and stops at the New Zealand border.

dead_ends.action: Tell a tourist or short-term visitor that any illness or hospital visit in New Zealand will be free or low-cost, as it would be in a universal-healthcare country
dead_ends.why_fails: New Zealand restricts publicly funded healthcare mostly to resident-class visa holders. People on temporary visit, study, or short work visas generally cannot access publicly funded care and are billed directly for GP visits, specialist care, and hospital stays for non-accident illness.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Visitors conflate ACC's no-fault accident cover, which does apply to them, with general public healthcare for illness, which mostly does not.

dead_ends.action: Assume any work visa qualifies for resident-level public healthcare access, regardless of how long the visa is valid for
dead_ends.why_fails: Work-visa holders only get resident-level access to publicly funded treatment if their visa permits a stay of 2 years or more, counted from their first day in New Zealand (or cumulative periods reaching 2 years including prior lawful stay). A work visa valid for under 2 years does not qualify, and the holder must pay for non-accident medical care.
dead_ends.condition: Work-visa holder whose visa is valid for less than 2 years from arrival

dead_ends.action: Treat ACC as a safety net that makes travel insurance optional, on the grounds that it covers visitors' injuries
dead_ends.why_fails: ACC covers treatment for accidental injury that happens in New Zealand, and nothing else. It does not cover illness or infection, it does not cover injuries that occur in transit to or from New Zealand, and it does not pay for emergency travel home or for rehabilitation once the visitor has left the country - the costs that most often turn a visitor's injury into a large bill.
dead_ends.common_misconception: ACC is well known as a government-run no-fault scheme, so it reads as general health insurance for visitors; it is accident-only and geographically bounded.

workarounds.action: Buy travel or health insurance before arrival for a visit, study, or short work visa; for longer work visas, confirm the visa's stated validity meets the 2-year threshold
workarounds.how: For visits or short stays, purchase travel insurance with medical cover before departure, since only ACC-covered accidents are treated free and all other treatment is billed. For work visas, check the visa grant letter for a stated validity of 2 years or more from the first day in New Zealand to qualify for resident-level publicly funded care; if it is shorter, budget for private cover or insurance instead.
workarounds.tradeoff: ACC covers accident-related injury treatment inside New Zealand regardless of visa status, so the policy's main job is illness cover - but ACC excludes in-transit injuries and repatriation, so dropping accident and evacuation cover entirely is not safe.

workarounds.action: If traveling from Australia or the UK, confirm what the reciprocal health agreement actually covers instead of assuming it substitutes for insurance
workarounds.how: Health New Zealand's reciprocal health agreements page sets out the scope: cover is limited to treatment that becomes immediately necessary during a temporary visit, not the full range a domestic patient receives, and it varies by treatment type.
workarounds.tradeoff: Reciprocal cover leaves the same gaps ACC does - routine care, ongoing treatment, and repatriation - so it narrows the insurance needed rather than removing it.
workarounds.condition: Traveler is an Australian or UK resident covered by a reciprocal agreement

frequently_confused_with.distinction: This canon covers eligibility for publicly funded healthcare for illness. ACC is a separate no-fault scheme that covers accident-related injury treatment for everyone regardless of visa status, and separately bars suing for compensatory damages.
